lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: point, line, distance, and arc as undefined starting terms
lessonRef.title: Concept model A: point, line, distance, and arc as undefined starting terms

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Study both examples. The second one drops some of the wording of the first.

items.prompt: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle. Central angle per side?
Why does the equilateral triangle construction work?

workedSolution.answer: All three sides equal the radius

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a circle?
choices: a shape whose area is πr²
a polygon with infinitely many sides
a closed curve with no corners
the set of all points in a plane at a fixed distance from a given centre point

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. Open the compass to more than half of AB. From A draw an arc above and below AB; from B, with the same opening, draw arcs crossing them. Draw the line through the two crossing points. What has been constructed?
choices: the angle bisector of ∠A
the perpendicular bisector of AB
a copy of segment AB
a line parallel to AB

items.prompt: A regular triangle is inscribed in a circle of radius 10. What central angle does each side subtend?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Which statement correctly justifies the perpendicular bisector construction?
choices: Both constructed points are equidistant from the endpoints, and the locus of such points is exactly the perpendicular bisector.
The arcs look symmetric, so the line must be perpendicular.
Any line through the midpoint is a perpendicular bisector.
The compass width was more than half the segment, which forces perpendicularity.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a perpendicular lines?
choices: two lines that form an isosceles triangle
two lines that never meet
two lines that intersect to form right angles
two lines with opposite slopes

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. With the compass set to the radius, mark successive arcs around the circle from a starting point, then join consecutive marks. What has been constructed?
choices: a regular hexagon inscribed in the circle
an equilateral triangle inscribed in the circle
a square inscribed in the circle
a regular pentagon inscribed in the circle

items.prompt: A regular triangle is inscribed in a circle of radius 11. What central angle does each side subtend?

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: Which statement correctly justifies the angle bisector construction?
choices: Equal arcs always produce equal angles regardless of the triangle.
The ray drawn appears to split the angle evenly.
The construction relies on the angle being acute.
The construction builds two congruent triangles by SSS, so the angles at the vertex are congruent.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a angle?
choices: the figure formed by two rays sharing a common endpoint
the amount of turn measured in degrees
the space between two intersecting lines
a corner of a polygon
